endpoints.name: Clients
endpoints.description: The client accounts under this Campaign Monitor login. AGENCIES ARE THE POINT OF THIS STRUCTURE: nearly every other endpoint takes a client id, and an account with several clients holds several entirely separate sets of lists, campaigns and subscribers. The first request in any question here.

endpoints.name: Billing details
endpoints.description: The account's billing state -- credits held and the plan in force. One record.

endpoints.name: Countries
endpoints.description: The country list Campaign Monitor accepts. Reference data.

endpoints.name: Timezones
endpoints.description: The timezone list Campaign Monitor accepts. Reference data, and relevant because a client's timezone determines how their timestamps read.

endpoints.name: Current date
endpoints.description: Campaign Monitor's own system date and time. Useful for anchoring a relative date range to the service's clock rather than the caller's.

endpoints.name: Administrators
endpoints.description: The administrators on the account, with name, email and status.

endpoints.name: Administrator details
endpoints.description: One administrator by email address.

endpoints.name: Primary contact
endpoints.description: The main contact for the whole account.

endpoints.name: Campaign summary
endpoints.description: The headline statistics of one campaign -- recipients, total and unique opens, clicks, unsubscribes, bounces, spam complaints and the web version views. Requires a campaign id. THE RIGHT ENDPOINT FOR A RATE: the detail endpoints below return one row per event and paging them to count is far more expensive than reading these totals.

endpoints.name: Campaign email client usage
endpoints.description: The email clients recipients opened one campaign in, with counts and percentages. Requires a campaign id. What a template has to render in -- and inferred from opens, so it describes the opening audience rather than the whole.

endpoints.name: Campaign lists and segments
endpoints.description: Which lists and segments one campaign was sent to. Requires a campaign id. The targeting record, which the campaign itself does not state.

endpoints.name: Campaign recipients
endpoints.description: Everyone one campaign was sent to, with their email and list. Requires a campaign id. The denominator, and the way to see which lists a campaign actually reached.

endpoints.name: Campaign bounces
endpoints.description: Bounce events, with the subscriber and the bounce type. Requires a campaign id. Hard and soft bounces mean different things and are distinguished here; treating them alike overstates list decay.

endpoints.name: Campaign opens
endpoints.description: Every open event for one campaign, with the subscriber, timestamp, IP and geolocation. Requires a campaign id. TOTAL opens including repeats -- the summary carries the unique figure. Carries the usual caveat that opens depend on images loading.

endpoints.name: Campaign clicks
endpoints.description: Every click event, with the subscriber, the URL clicked, timestamp and geolocation. Requires a campaign id. The sounder engagement signal, and the URL column is what says which content drew the response.

endpoints.name: Campaign unsubscribes
endpoints.description: Unsubscribe events attributable to one campaign, with timestamps. Requires a campaign id. The per-send cost of a campaign.

endpoints.name: Campaign spam complaints
endpoints.description: Spam complaints from one campaign. Requires a campaign id. Small numbers matter -- a handful is enough to affect deliverability for everything sent afterwards.

endpoints.name: Client's details
endpoints.description: One client's settings -- company, timezone, country, and their billing and permission configuration. Requires a client id. THE TIMEZONE MATTERS: campaign and subscriber timestamps are returned in the client's own timezone, so figures from two clients are not on the same clock.

endpoints.name: Sent campaigns
endpoints.description: The campaigns one client has actually sent, with name, subject, sent date, the number of recipients, and the web version url. Requires a client id. The starting point for reporting: only sent campaigns have statistics, and the campaign id here is what every report endpoint below takes.

endpoints.name: Scheduled campaigns
endpoints.description: Campaigns queued to send, with their scheduled date. Requires a client id. Forward-looking; no statistics exist yet.

endpoints.name: Draft campaigns
endpoints.description: Campaigns not yet scheduled. Requires a client id. Counting all three campaign endpoints together counts work that was never sent.

endpoints.name: Subscriber lists
endpoints.description: The subscriber lists belonging to one client. Requires a client id. The audience container; subscribers belong to a list rather than to the client, so the same person on two lists is two subscriber records.

endpoints.name: Lists for an email address
endpoints.description: Which of a client's lists one email address appears on, and in what state. Requires the client id and email. The answer to why someone did or did not receive a send.

endpoints.name: Segments
endpoints.description: All segments across one client's lists. Requires a client id.

endpoints.name: Suppression list
endpoints.description: Addresses suppressed across one client -- never mailed regardless of list. Requires a client id. The explanation for a send reaching fewer people than the list size.

endpoints.name: Templates
endpoints.description: The email templates belonging to one client. Requires a client id.

endpoints.name: People
endpoints.description: The users belonging to one client, with their access level. Requires a client id. Client-level access, as opposed to account-level administrators.

endpoints.name: Person details
endpoints.description: One client user by email address. Requires the client id.

endpoints.name: Client's primary contact
endpoints.description: The main contact for one client.

endpoints.name: Journeys
endpoints.description: The automated journeys defined for one client. Requires a client id. Journeys send over time in response to behaviour, so their sends are separate from campaigns entirely -- an email volume figure taken from campaigns alone omits everything automation sent.

endpoints.name: Journey summary
endpoints.description: One journey's structure and its aggregate performance. Requires a journey id. The email ids here are what the journey report endpoints take.

endpoints.name: Journey email recipients
endpoints.description: Who one journey email was sent to. Requires the email id.

endpoints.name: Journey email opens
endpoints.description: Open events for one journey email. Requires the email id.

endpoints.name: Journey email clicks
endpoints.description: Click events for one journey email. Requires the email id.

endpoints.name: Journey email bounces
endpoints.description: Bounce events for one journey email. Requires the email id.

endpoints.name: Journey email unsubscribes
endpoints.description: Unsubscribe events attributable to one journey email. Requires the email id.

endpoints.name: List details
endpoints.description: One list's settings -- name, confirmation requirements and the unsubscribe behaviour. Requires a list id. THE UNSUBSCRIBE SETTING MATTERS: a list set to unsubscribe from all client lists behaves very differently from one that unsubscribes only from itself, which explains audience losses that no single campaign accounts for.

endpoints.name: List stats
endpoints.description: The counts of one list -- active, unconfirmed, bounced, unsubscribed and deleted subscribers, with the new-subscriber and unsubscribe totals for the period. Requires a list id. A ready-made summary; the five state endpoints below are the row-level detail.

endpoints.name: List custom fields
endpoints.description: The custom fields defined on one list, with their names and types. Requires a list id. The decoder for custom values on subscribers, and note fields are PER LIST -- the same attribute on two lists is two definitions.

endpoints.name: List segments
endpoints.description: The segments defined on one list, with their rules. Requires a list id.

endpoints.name: Active subscribers
endpoints.description: The subscribers on one list who can be mailed, optionally added since a date. Requires a list id. THE ONLY MAILABLE STATE -- the four endpoints below hold the rest, and a subscriber count taken from the list without regard to state overstates reach.

endpoints.name: Unconfirmed subscribers
endpoints.description: Subscribers who signed up but never confirmed, on a confirmed-opt-in list. They are not mailable and are not opt-outs either -- they are a signup funnel leak, and counting them as lost subscribers misattributes the cause.

endpoints.name: Unsubscribed subscribers
endpoints.description: Subscribers who opted out, with the date. The deliberate departures.

endpoints.name: Bounced subscribers
endpoints.description: Subscribers removed for bouncing. Address decay rather than a decision, which is why it should be separated from unsubscribes when explaining audience shrinkage.

endpoints.name: Deleted subscribers
endpoints.description: Subscribers removed from the list by an administrator.

endpoints.name: List webhooks
endpoints.description: The webhooks configured on one list. Requires a list id. Integration configuration.

endpoints.name: Testing a webhook
endpoints.description: Fires a test payload at one webhook and reports the result. Requires the list and webhook ids. A diagnostic action rather than data.

endpoints.name: Segment's details
endpoints.description: One segment's rules and its current subscriber count. Requires a segment id. The rules state the client's own definition of the audience, which the name rarely conveys.

endpoints.name: Segment's active subsribers
endpoints.description: The mailable subscribers currently matching one segment. Requires a segment id. Evaluated at request time, so it can differ from the count the segment reports.

endpoints.name: Subscriber's details
endpoints.description: One subscriber on one list, by email, optionally with their tracking history. Requires the list id and email.

endpoints.name: Subscriber's history
endpoints.description: Every action one subscriber took across campaigns -- opens, clicks, unsubscribes -- with timestamps. Requires the list id and email. THE PER-PERSON ENGAGEMENT RECORD, which no campaign report gives, and the basis for identifying a lapsing subscriber.

endpoints.name: Template
endpoints.description: One template by id, with its content and screenshot.

endpoints.name: Smart email listing
endpoints.description: The transactional smart emails defined, by status. Transactional sends are a separate product from campaigns and journeys, with their own statistics -- a complete picture of email volume needs all three.

endpoints.name: Smart email details
endpoints.description: One smart email by id, with its content and settings.

endpoints.name: Classic email group listing
endpoints.description: The classic transactional email groups for one client.

endpoints.name: Statistics
endpoints.description: Transactional email statistics -- sent, delivered, bounced, opened and clicked -- over a period, optionally for one smart email. The aggregate view of transactional sending.

endpoints.name: Message timeline
endpoints.suffix: /v3.2/transactional/messages?status={Status?}&count={Count?}&sentBeforeID={Sent Before ID?}&sentAfterID={Sent After ID?}&smartEmailID={Smart Email ID?}&group={Group?}&clientID={Client ID?}
endpoints.description: Individual transactional messages with their status, filterable by status and count. The per-message record, as opposed to the aggregate.

endpoints.name: Message details
endpoints.description: One transactional message by id, optionally with its statistics. Where a specific message's delivery is traced.
